```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, results = "asis")
r  <- params$report
d  <- r$days
s  <- r$settings
sl <- setNames(as.list(r$sleep$mean), r$sleep$var)
tm <- r$timing
ds <- r$daysum
dsm <- setNames(as.list(ds$mean), ds$var)
dom <- attr(ds, "domains")
coh <- r$coherence
dates <- range(d$date, na.rm = TRUE)
has_sleep <- r$n_nights > 0
has_diary <- r$n_diary > 0
note <- function(x) cat(sprintf('<p class="note">%s</p>', x))
```

<header class="hero">
<img class="logo" src="rth_logo.png" alt="Rise to Health, a Carnegie Mellon University study">
<h1>Your daily patterns</h1>
```{r}
cat(sprintf('<p class="dates">%s to %s &middot; %d diary days &middot; %d nights with the watch</p>',
            format(dates[1], "%B %d"), format(dates[2], "%B %d, %Y"), r$n_diary, r$n_nights))
```
</header>

<section class="intro">
<p><strong>Thank you for completing the daily assessments!</strong> For about two weeks you wore a sleep watch and told us about your days. This report shows your specific patterns, but since we&rsquo;re researchers, not medical doctors, we can&rsquo;t give health advice or interpretations.</p>
</section>

<section id="highlights" class="highlights">
<h2>Your highlights</h2>
```{r}
cat(highlights_html(r))
```
<p class="hl-more">Want the full story? Keep scrolling for your full report.</p>
</section>

<h2 class="part">Your full report</h2>

<section id="days">
<h2>Your days</h2>
```{r}
if (!has_diary) {
  note("We didn't receive enough nightly diaries to show this section.")
} else {
  cat('<h3>Your events</h3>')
  cat("<p>Each night you told us what happened that day. Here's what a typical day looked like for you, and how much that changed from day to day.</p>")
  cat(events_glance_html(r))
  cat(sources_html(dom))
  cat('<h3 id="mood">Your mood</h3>')
  raw <- function(x) format(round(1 + 4 * x / 100, 1), nsmall = 1)
  cat(sprintf("<p>You also rated how you felt each day, from 1 (lowest) to 5 (highest). Your negative mood (like sad, worried, or lonely) averaged <strong>%s</strong>, and your positive mood (like happy, calm, or close to others) averaged <strong>%s</strong>.</p>",
              raw(dsm$neg_pomp), raw(dsm$pos_pomp)))
  cat(img_tag(plot_mood(d), height = 2.5, alt = "Daily mood ratings"))
  if (isTRUE(r$trigger$triggered)) {
    cat('<div class="support-box"><p><strong>You told us that many of your days felt hard.</strong> That\'s worth paying attention to, and you don\'t have to handle it alone. Talking with someone you trust can help, and there are free, confidential resources you can reach any time.</p><p><a href="#support">See the support resources at the end of this report</a>.</p></div>')
  }
}
```
</section>

<section id="mood-links">
<h2>How your events and mood went together</h2>
```{r}
ml <- r$mood_links
n_pair_mood <- sum(!is.na(d$stress_n) & !is.na(d$neg_pomp))
if (n_pair_mood < s$min_days) {
  note(sprintf("We need at least %d diary days to look at these patterns, and we have %d from you. Thanks for the ones you did complete!",
               s$min_days, n_pair_mood))
}
ttl <- c(stress_n = "Unpleasant events", pos_n = "Positive events", help_n = "Helping others")
if (n_pair_mood >= s$min_days) {
  cat("<p>Each bar shows how your mood tended to compare with your typical on days with <strong>one more</strong> event. Bars inside the grey zone mean &ldquo;about the same.&rdquo;</p>")
  cat(img_tag(plot_mood_change(ml, s$same_band[["neg_pomp"]]), height = 3.4,
              alt = "Change in mood on days with one more event"))
  if (any(ml$capped %in% TRUE & ml$status == "shown")) cat(cap_note)
  cat('<div class="callout"><p><strong>Did you know?</strong> Two people can go through the exact same thing and feel totally different about it. A fight with a friend might ruin one person&rsquo;s whole day, while someone else shakes it off by lunch. Neither is right or wrong; that&rsquo;s just how different people are. Scientists are even curious whether these differences might go along with differences in health, which is one of the things Rise to Health is studying. These bars show how <em>your</em> mood tended to move with your days.</p><p><strong>What this can and can&rsquo;t tell you.</strong> These bars show what happened on the same days, not what caused what. For example, if you were in a better mood on days you helped others, helping may have lifted your mood, or you may have been more likely to help when you were already in a good mood.</p></div>')
}
```
</section>

<section id="sleep">
<h2>Your sleep at a glance</h2>
```{r}
if (!has_sleep) {
  note("We didn't get usable sleep watch data for your nights, so this section is empty.")
} else {
  cat('<p>Here&rsquo;s how you slept, along with what the National Sleep Foundation (NSF) recommends where it has a recommendation.</p>')
  cat(glance_html(r))
}
```
</section>

<section id="nights">
<h2>Night to night</h2>
```{r}
if (has_sleep) {
  cat('<p>Sleep bounces around from night to night for everyone. Here&rsquo;s how yours moved! Each dot is one of your nights, the dashed line is your average, and the peach bands are the NSF reference ranges for good or typical sleep. How many of your dots landed in the peach zone?</p>')
  cat(img_tag(plot_nights(d, r$guideline, s$ref_se_min, s$ref_sol_max), height = 3.2, alt = "Sleep measures across nights"))
} else {
  note("No sleep watch data to show here.")
}
```
</section>

<section id="sleep-links">
<h2>How your events and that night&rsquo;s sleep went together</h2>
```{r}
sk <- r$sleep_links
n_pair_sleep <- sum(!is.na(d$stress_n) & !is.na(d$tst))
enough <- n_pair_sleep >= s$min_days
if (!enough) {
  note(sprintf("We need at least %d days with both a diary and a night of sleep watch data to look at these patterns, and we have %d from you.",
               s$min_days, n_pair_sleep))
  cat(redo_offer_html(params$contact))
}
if (enough) cat(events_sleep_html(r))
```
</section>

<section id="note">
<h2>A note on these numbers</h2>
<p>This report describes about two weeks of your own days, so your patterns might look different over another two weeks. We did not run statistical tests on one person&rsquo;s data, so these patterns are descriptions of what happened, not proof that one thing affects another. When we looked at how things went together, we also softened any very unusual day or night a little, so that a single one doesn&rsquo;t decide the whole pattern.</p>
<p>When we combine data from all the teens in Rise to Health, we can test questions like these for teens in general, and then look at how they relate to everyone&rsquo;s blood work to see which ones matter for heart health. Those are the findings we&rsquo;ll share in our scientific publications. Stay tuned!</p>
</section>
